title: Design Search Autocomplete / Typeahead
prompt: Design the search autocomplete system that suggests completions as a user types — like the dropdown under a search box. For each keystroke it should return the top few most relevant suggestions for the current prefix, extremely fast, at web scale.
blurb: Trie-based top-k over prefixes: precomputation, sharding, ranking, and single-digit-millisecond latency.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (top-k suggestions per prefix, freshness, personalization) from non-functional (very low latency, high availability, scale).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about number of suggestions, latency budget, ranking signal, freshness, personalization, languages.

rubric.label: Estimations
rubric.description: Estimates query QPS (per keystroke), unique prefixes/terms, trie memory, update volume.

rubric.label: Core data structure (trie)
rubric.description: Trie/prefix tree with precomputed top-k per node; why not query at read time; memory vs compute tradeoff.

rubric.label: Top-k & ranking
rubric.description: Ranking by frequency/recency/personalization; storing top-k at each node; how top-k is aggregated bottom-up.

rubric.label: API design
rubric.description: GET /suggest?q=prefix contract, debounce, response shape, prefix normalization.

rubric.label: High-level design
rubric.description: Read path (edge/cache → trie service) separated from the offline pipeline that builds/updates the trie from query logs.

rubric.label: Prefix sharding & scaling
rubric.description: Sharding the trie by prefix, hot-prefix balancing, replication, keeping shards in memory.

rubric.label: Freshness / update pipeline
rubric.description: Aggregating query logs, rebuilding/patching the trie, trending terms, batch vs incremental updates.

rubric.label: Latency engineering
rubric.description: Debouncing, caching popular prefixes at the edge, in-memory serving, avoiding per-keystroke DB hits.

rubric.label: Observability
rubric.description: Suggest latency, cache hit ratio, click-through on suggestions, trie build lag.

functional_requirements: Return top-k (e.g. 5-10) suggestions for a typed prefix
Update suggestions as new queries trend (freshness)
nonfunctional_requirements: Very low latency — < 50-100ms end-to-end per keystroke (ideally single-digit ms server side)
Extremely high read QPS (a query = many keystrokes)
High availability; stale suggestions acceptable briefly
Scales to hundreds of millions of terms
clarifying_questions: What's the latency budget per keystroke?
Ranking signal — global popularity, recency, personalization?
How fresh must trending terms be — minutes or a day?
qualifying_questions: Do we suggest full queries (search-log driven) or dictionary terms?
Is personalization in scope for v1 or later?

estimations.traffic: 10B searches/day, ~20 keystrokes each → ~200B suggest calls/day ≈ ~2.3M QPS; debounce cuts this materially
estimations.terms: ~100M-1B unique query strings; store top-k per prefix node in a trie
estimations.memory: Trie with precomputed top-k per node for 100M+ terms → tens of GB per full copy; shard + replicate across memory
estimations.updates: Aggregate query logs hourly/daily; incremental trending updates more frequently

data_model: trie nodes: each node = prefix; stores precomputed top-k {term, score} for that subtree
term_frequency(term, count, last_seen) aggregated from logs
prefix_cache: prefix → top-k suggestions (edge/Redis, short TTL)
trie shards keyed by prefix range or first-N chars
api_design: Client debounces (~100-300ms) and cancels stale in-flight requests
Prefix normalized (lowercase, trim, unicode-fold) before lookup
reference.high_level_design: The read path is engineered for latency: the client debounces keystrokes and calls /suggest; an edge/prefix cache answers the most popular prefixes; misses hit the in-memory trie service. The trie is precomputed so that each node already stores the top-k completions for its subtree — a lookup is O(prefix length) to walk to the node, then return its stored top-k, with no read-time aggregation. The trie is sharded by prefix across many in-memory replicas. Separately, an offline pipeline consumes query logs (Kafka), aggregates term frequencies with recency weighting, recomputes top-k per node, and ships a new trie (full rebuild periodically + incremental patches for trending terms) to the serving replicas. Personalization, when enabled, re-ranks the global top-k with per-user signals.

deep_dives.probe: Why precompute top-k at every trie node instead of walking the subtree at query time? Walk me through the memory-vs-latency tradeoff and how you aggregate top-k bottom-up when building the trie.
Two terms share a prefix. How do you rank them — frequency, recency, both? How is the top-k at a parent node derived from its children, and how big does k need to be at each node?
The trie doesn't fit on one box, and prefixes like 'a' are far hotter than 'z'. How do you shard so no single shard is overloaded, and how do you route a lookup to the right shard?
A term suddenly trends (breaking news). Your trie was built this morning. How do you surface it within minutes without a full rebuild — incremental patch, overlay, or streaming update?
You must answer per keystroke in single-digit ms. What do you cache at the edge, how does debounce help, and how do you keep DB/disk entirely off the read path?
You cache top-k per popular prefix with a short TTL. When a very hot prefix's cache entry expires under 2M QPS, how do you prevent a stampede onto the trie service?

Query events land in a datastore/log. How do you feed the trie-build and trending pipelines off it — change data capture with Debezium, or streaming the query log directly? How do you weight recency vs total frequency?

followup_bank.question: Do you store the top-k completions at each node or compute them at read time? Justify the memory cost of precomputation.
How is a node's top-k derived from its children's top-k during the build, and how large must k be at intermediate nodes to stay correct?
Prefixes are wildly skewed (many words start with 's', few with 'x'). How do you shard the trie to balance load and route lookups?
What's the eviction/TTL for the prefix cache, and how do you avoid a stampede when a hot prefix's entry expires under millions of QPS?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions database or logs or store
followup_bank.question: How do you feed the trie-build pipeline from query logs — CDC/Debezium vs streaming — and how do you incorporate recency vs raw frequency?
How do you surface a newly trending term within minutes without rebuilding the whole trie?
Where does debouncing happen, and how do you guarantee no disk/DB access on the per-keystroke read path?

scaling: Keep the trie fully in memory; shard by prefix across replicas
Replicate hot shards to spread skewed prefix load
Edge/CDN caching of the hottest prefixes with short TTLs
Client debounce + request cancellation to cut effective QPS
Separate the heavy offline build pipeline from the light read path
bottlenecks: Read-path latency under millions of QPS
Skewed prefix distribution creating hot shards
Trie memory footprint at hundreds of millions of terms
Rebuild lag limiting freshness for trending terms
tradeoffs: Precomputed top-k per node (fast reads, more memory + build cost) vs read-time aggregation (less memory, slower)
Full periodic rebuild (simple, stale between builds) vs incremental streaming updates (fresh, complex)
Global ranking (cacheable, shared) vs personalized (fresh per user, uncacheable)
Larger k at nodes (more correct merges, more memory) vs smaller k
alternative_solutions: Elasticsearch/inverted-index completion suggester instead of a bespoke trie
FST (finite state transducer) for compact prefix storage
Ternary search tree for memory efficiency over a plain trie
Precomputed prefix→top-k KV map (no tree) served from an in-memory store for a bounded prefix set
observability: Trie build lag and freshness of trending terms
security: Filter offensive/unsafe or private strings out of the suggestion set
Rate-limit the suggest endpoint to prevent scraping/abuse
Avoid leaking other users' private queries via personalization
Sanitize/normalize input to prevent injection into logs/index
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer builds around a trie with precomputed top-k completions stored at every node, so a per-keystroke lookup is just an O(prefix-length) walk returning the node's stored list — no read-time aggregation. It explains the memory-vs-latency tradeoff of precomputation, how a node's top-k is merged bottom-up from its children during an offline build, and how the trie is sharded by prefix (with hot-prefix replication) and kept fully in memory. It separates the light read path — client debounce, edge prefix cache, in-memory serving with no disk/DB on the path — from the heavy offline pipeline that aggregates query logs (with recency weighting) and rebuilds/patches the trie, plus an incremental path for trending terms. It proactively raises read-path latency, prefix skew/hot shards, trie memory, and rebuild-freshness as the main bottlenecks, and addresses cache stampede on hot prefixes and personalization's uncacheable cost.

interviewer_notes: The core signal is realizing you must precompute top-k at each trie node rather than aggregate at read time — steer them there if they propose scanning subtrees per query. Then push on how top-k merges bottom-up during the build and how big k must be. Prefix skew (hot shards) is the key scaling probe; make them balance/route. Freshness for trending terms separates good from great — force an incremental-update story, not just 'rebuild nightly'. This is latency-obsessed: interrupt any design that touches disk/DB on the keystroke path. If they mention a query-log datastore, fire the CDC/Debezium probe; if they add a prefix cache, fire the eviction/stampede probe.
